title: Capacity Utilization and Efficiency Metrics
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/01 - Capacity Utilization and Efficiency Metrics.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to determine how efficiently a chemical production facility is utilizing its available capacity and resources.
dataRequired: Maximum production capacity (tons or units per time period, e.g., per day, month, or year)
Actual production output (tons or units produced during the same time period)
Downtime data (planned and unplanned)
Operational hours available versus operational hours used
improve: Reduce Downtime through predictive and preventive maintenance programs, targeting both planned and unplanned downtime reduction.
Optimize Batch Sizes to better match production runs with demand, reducing overproduction and waste.
Improve Scheduling and Planning by using production planning software to manage capacity more dynamically.
Invest in Staff Training and Automation to reduce human error and improve process automation, which can increase output without additional capacity.

Consider Process Optimization and Innovation, such as using advanced catalysts or modifying production processes to boost reaction speeds or yields, thus increasing throughput without additional capacity.
How to Analyze a Chemicals Company

formulas.source: CUR = (Actual Production Output / Maximum Production Capacity) x 100
Downtime Impact (%) = (Downtime Hours / Total Operational Hours) x 100

formulas.output: How to Analyze a Chemicals Company For example, Energy Efficiency
formulas.source: How to Analyze a Chemicals Company For example, Energy Efficiency = (Total Energy Consumed / Actual Production Output)

sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/36 - Feedstock Dependency, Cost, Sourcing, and Substitution.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the company’s dependency on key feedstocks, assess feedstock costs and sourcing strategies, and explore substitution options.
dataRequired: List of primary feedstocks, quantities used, and costs
Dependency levels for each feedstock, including single-sourced or multi-sourced materials
Historical and forecasted price data for feedstocks
Supplier contracts and terms, including exclusivity, pricing, and lead times
Alternative feedstock options and associated costs
Quality and performance implications of feedstock substitutions
Environmental and regulatory factors influencing feedstock selection
Industry benchmarks for feedstock costs, dependency levels, and substitution strategies
improve: Implement Cost Hedging or Long-term Contracts

title: Supply Chain Integration and Logistics Optimization
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/37 - Supply Chain Integration and Logistics Optimization.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the integration of supply chain processes and optimize logistics to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance responsiveness.
dataRequired: Current supply chain workflow (from procurement to distribution) and key processes
Lead times, transit times, and order cycle times for each supply chain stage
Cost data for procurement, warehousing, and transportation
Inventory levels and turnover rates
Supplier reliability and on-time delivery rates
Customer demand variability and order patterns
Technology and digital tools in use for supply chain management (e.g., ERP, TMS, WMS)
Industry benchmarks for supply chain efficiency and logistics costs

title: Supplier Dependence and Diversification Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/38 - Supplier Dependence and Diversification Analysis.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the company’s dependence on key suppliers and assess diversification levels within the supply chain.
dataRequired: List of key suppliers by product or material, including primary feedstocks and critical components
Spend allocation per supplier (percentage of total procurement spend)
Supplier performance metrics (e.g., on-time delivery rate, quality issues)
Geographic location of suppliers and associated geopolitical or environmental risks
Contract terms, including exclusivity clauses and lead times
Potential alternative suppliers and their capacity, quality, and costs
Industry benchmarks for supplier diversification and risk management

title: Global Trade Flow Analysis for Raw Materials and Finished Products
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/39 - Global Trade Flow Analysis for Raw Materials and Finished.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to assess the flow of raw materials and finished products across global markets, identifying key trade routes, dependencies, and potential risks.
dataRequired: Origin and destination data for raw materials and finished products
Trade routes and transportation modes used for each flow
Volume, frequency, and cost data associated with each trade route
Import/export tariffs, trade agreements, and regulatory requirements by country
Lead times and transit times for each route
Geopolitical risks and recent disruptions impacting trade routes
Industry benchmarks for trade flow efficiency and costs

title: Supplier Quality and Consistency Impact Assessment
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/40 - Supplier Quality and Consistency Impact Assessment.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the quality and consistency of materials provided by suppliers, assessing their impact on production efficiency, product quality, and customer satisfaction.
dataRequired: Quality control metrics for each supplier, including defect rates and compliance with specifications
Frequency of quality issues or deviations in supplied materials
Historical data on production downtime or delays caused by supplier issues
Cost of quality issues (e.g., rework, scrap, warranty claims)
Customer complaints or returns linked to supplier-related quality issues
Supplier performance metrics, including on-time delivery and responsiveness
Industry benchmarks for supplier quality and consistency

title: Vertical Integration Opportunities and Value Chain Positioning
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/chemical/41 - Vertical Integration Opportunities and Value Chain Positioning.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to assess opportunities for vertical integration within the value chain to enhance control over inputs, reduce costs, improve product quality, and capture additional value.
dataRequired: Current value chain map, detailing suppliers, production, distribution, and sales channels
Costs associated with sourcing, production, and distribution stages
Supplier performance data, including quality, cost consistency, and reliability
Market analysis for upstream (e.g., raw materials, components) and downstream (e.g., distribution, sales) integration opportunities
Competitor analysis on integration strategies and value chain positioning
Customer demand trends and preferences related to control over product quality, supply reliability, and sustainability
Capital investment requirements and potential ROI for integration initiatives
Regulatory and industry constraints or incentives for vertical integration
